reason: r33 replaces r32, which was packaged and never run, and starts from r31's behaviour. The glow write is reverted: the glow keeps its visibility bit and the mask clips it along with the bar, which is what the design asks for (clip it, never hide it). The clip box is fed sharpness_gauge_core::prototype_ratio, the plan's Phase 2 fixed ratios 0/25/50/100% at 20 s each, read from this thread's own update count (60 ticks ≈ 1 s, the divider lib.rs's clip probe logs at). The live ratio stays computed in the mask's enter hook and is unused. One line per change of the forced ratio prints the ratio_bp, the box written, and the bar's +0xe0, +0xf0 and +0x10c rectangles: the offsets core/src/lib.rs already reads, nothing new. Forced ratios answer r31. That run (NRO 88e63e7575534cf21a160aaf7e76e2ca6d89e1214c7c58563430dbff92a3f77b installed matching, log work/modern-sharpness-gauge/runs/r31-eden-2026-10-24.txt) showed the setter applying our rectangle in screen coordinates and moving with the ratio (339 -> 322 px), and the user reported no visual difference from vanilla. The lowest ratio that hunt reached is 8771 basis points. mask_box scales the sprite's ink columns 18..79 of 88 into the node rect 110..238, the default core/src/lib.rs calls unproven, so a live hunt may never put the cut inside the drawn blade. The fixed steps put the cut at the ink's left edge, a quarter, a half and its right edge, where the eye can see it.
runtime_test: NOT RUN. Pass, on screen: the bar steps through empty, a quarter, half and full, 20 seconds on each, with the cut at the sword ink's left edge, a quarter, a half and its right edge, and a screenshot at each step showing where the cut falls on the blade. The bar is there from the quest start and survives an area change, as in the r30/r31 runs. In the log: one forced-ratio line per step with the box and the bar's three rectangles, and the glow counted visible again in the sample lines, since r33 does not touch its visibility bit. Gameplay NOT RUN.

r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r25 has not been run. r24's run drew the gauge from the quest start and lost it at an area change, where a mask kept clipping after its links broke; the disable-on-loss path has no runtime evidence, and a mask inserted into a second area's row has never been observed (r24's log ends 12 s after the transition, gauge HUD absent)
